research_notes: Initial research 2026-10-01: frozen extract, two historical parliamentary handbooks, official biography, first speech, 2013 network paper, 2014 employer conference program, SYC history and first-person parliamentary reference, and 2015/2018 reporting reviewed. Explicit part-time advising retained; no substantive full-time interval established.

Priority gaps: names and appointment chronology of law firms, public professional CV, employer-specific hours and leave; legal researcher versus later adviser roles; Youth Connections payroll entity and contract; SYC/HYPA transition and cessation; government appointment and resignation dates. Preserve month precision for April 2012; do not convert program funding cessation into a personal exit.

Political dates 2006 (Redmond), 2008 (Briggs) and a six-month Briggs duration appeared in secondary summaries; underlying full primary/press evidence not obtained, so not promoted to dated spells. Redmond opposition leadership title must not be backdated merely from later biography. Named employers are independently corroborated.

Historical employer annual-report avenue: ChangePath SYC listing linked 2014 report https://www.syc.net.au/app/uploads/2018/06/5432-SYC-Annual-Report_OUT2A_WEB-2014.pdf and 2015 report https://www.syc.net.au/app/uploads/2018/06/6989-SYC-Annual-Report_OUT2_LR-2015.pdf . Both returned 404 Not Found. Seek relocated SYC archive or contemporaneous ACNC report without bypassing access controls.

Other source gaps: direct LinkedIn profile https://au.linkedin.com/in/rebekha-sharkie-5690586b returned 429 Too Many Requests; not retried this cycle. Jobs Australia program direct PDF 403, APH direct biography Internal Error; public indexed extracts and historical handbooks supplied usable alternatives. Namesake Rebecca Sharkie marketing profiles not attributed.

Education dates and any work before/alongside study remain unverified. First speech refers to work while parenting but does not prove full-time status or provide dated leave. Employment during the May–July 2018 parliamentary break is unknown; no assumption of zero.
Last follow-up 2026-10-01. Next initial member Marielle Smith; return after nationwide initial coverage with law-firm, SYC and government appointment leads.
